errorCodes.meaning: The recipient holds no key by that identifier, or the key is not one its caller may name.
`actions` was empty. An empty grant confers nothing rather than everything, and is refused rather than interpreted.

Ext.description: Vendor-namespaced extension object per SPEC.md §4.5.1. Each immediate key MUST be a reverse-DNS namespace; structure under each namespace is opaque to the framework.
Ext.title: Ext

Purpose.description: What content is used for: a lowerCamelCase name registered in the VTI specification's purpose registry (Appendix H) — `personalisation`, `taskExecution`, `analytics`, `modelTraining` at the time of writing — or an absolute IRI naming a purpose defined elsewhere, such as a purpose of the W3C Data Privacy Vocabulary (`https://w3id.org/dpv#ServicePersonalisation`). Compared by exact string equality: a consumer MUST NOT treat a purpose it does not recognise as equal to any other, and grants only a request naming exactly a listed purpose (VTI-ACL-109). A registered name is never an IRI, because it contains no `:`.
Purpose.title: Purpose

PurposeScope.description: An explicit purpose scope. Exactly one of two shapes, discriminated by `scope`: `any`, or `listed` with a NON-EMPTY list of purposes. The empty list is invalid, not a third shape.
PurposeScope.title: PurposeScope

PurposeScopeAny.description: Any purpose except `modelTraining` (training, fine-tuning or evaluating a machine-learning model on the content), which `any` never grants (VTI-ACL-105).
PurposeScopeAny.title: PurposeScopeAny

PurposeScopeListed.description: Exactly the listed purposes. A request naming any other purpose is refused.

purposes.description: Non-empty set of purposes. An empty array is invalid (it is not `any`).

PurposeScopeListed.title: PurposeScopeListed

Response.title: Rooms Owner Issue Authority — response payload

actions.description: What the subject may do. MUST NOT be empty — an empty list confers nothing rather than everything, and a schema that allowed it would make the more dangerous reading available to a careless consumer. `curate` is not implied by `write`: pinning, deprecating and retracting are judgements over shared knowledge, not writes.

purposes.description: OPTIONAL. What the subject may use the content it reads under this grant for (VTI-ACL-110): `{"scope": "any"}` or a non-empty list. Stated in the credential exactly as given; absent, the credential states none, which grants `any` — never `modelTraining`, which a grant must name.

roomId.description: The room whose identity issues this credential. The recipient MUST hold a signing key for it — it is signing AS the room, not as itself.

signingKeyId.description: Which held key signs. Named explicitly rather than looked up from `roomId`, because nothing maps a DID to a key it was minted with and inventing that mapping would add a lifecycle to get wrong. A key that is not the room's produces a credential that fails to verify against the room's DID document — loud, and at the first use rather than later.

subject.description: The party this grants to. A chain ROOT: the room is the governing party, so this is the grant everything else descends from. A holder narrows their own grant with attenuation instead, which needs no issuer.

validUntil.description: When the grant lapses. REQUIRED, and not merely recommended: nothing about the subject's current standing is consulted when an authority credential is verified, so a grant that never expires is authority nobody can withdraw by waiting. A verifier refuses a chain link carrying none, so a grant minted without one could not have been used. Changing what a party may do reissues this one small credential and leaves the membership edge alone, which is why the two are separate credentials.
